statement: There are 666,841,088 nonsingular complex quadrics tangent to nine general quadrics in P³.

answer.text: On the space of complete quadrics in P3, a quadric-tangency condition has divisor class q=2(p+l+h), where p,l,h impose incidence with a point, tangency to a line, and tangency to a plane. Consequently nine general quadric-tangency conditions have q^9=2^9 sum_(alpha+beta+gamma=9) [9!/(alpha!beta!gamma!)] p^alpha l^beta h^gamma=666841088 nonsingular complex solutions.

notes:
Total reality for this nine-quadric problem is an aim, not a result of the paper.

Imported from the 2026-10-26 catalogue record R_8307a860c8d9b807; the source claim has not been newly rechecked against the paper for this beta import.

Schubert 1879, §22 and p.106, is explicitly credited for these numerical counts. Brysiewicz–Fevola–Sturmfels provide the supporting article for their polynomial/prime-ideal formulation and modern verification; their certified real constructions are separate results.
